chunks: And it was narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
A man stood before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: I divorced my wife for the ʿiddah without witnesses.
So he said: Your divorce is not a divorce; therefore return to your family.

key_terms.أَهْلِكَ: your family; here referring to his wife/household to whom he is told to return
key_terms.امْرَأَتِي: my wife; the spouse being divorced
key_terms.شُهُودٍ: witnesses; those whose presence is required for validity
key_terms.طَلَاقُكَ: your divorce; the divorce pronouncement under question
key_terms.طَلَّقْتُ: I divorced; the act of pronouncing divorce
key_terms.لِلْعِدَّةِ: for the waiting period; in the context of divorce procedure connected to ʿiddah

ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid without witnesses in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a divorce pronounced without witnesses is not valid. It highlights the importance of proper procedure in divorce and preserves family order according to the sunnah.
